falsifier: A graph and vertex partition violating the displayed bound.
proof:
Give the parts of \(\mathcal P\) distinct binary codes in \(2^\mu\).
For each edge joining distinct parts, use the least coordinate at which the
two part codes differ. For a fixed coordinate, all assigned edges cross the
bipartition determined by that coordinate's bit, so the cross-part graph is
covered by \(\mu\) bipartite layers. The graph containing only edges internal
to the parts is a disjoint union of the graphs \(G[P]\), so its triangle-cover
number is the supremum of their triangle-cover numbers by T4. Combine the two
covers.
statement:
Let \(G\) be a graph, let \(\mathcal P\) be a partition of \(V(G)\), and let
\(\mu\) be a cardinal for which \(|\mathcal P|\le 2^\mu\). Then
\[
tc(G)\le \mu+\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}tc(G[P]).
\]
title: Vertex-Partition Compression Inequality

falsifier: A cover of a high-cover edge set by at most κ edge sets, all κ-coverable.
proof:
If every \(F_i\) had triangle-cover number at most \(\kappa\), their union
would belong to the \(\kappa\)-complete edge ideal \(\mathcal I_\kappa(G)\)
by T1, contradicting \(tc(G)>\kappa\).
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite and \(tc(G)>\kappa\). If
\[
E(G)=\bigcup_{i\in I}F_i,\qquad |I|\le\kappa,
\]
then \(tc((V(G),F_i))>\kappa\) for at least one \(i\).
title: Edge-Partition Self-Similarity

falsifier: A first stage α<κ⁺ at which the cumulative κ-null edge deletion destroys positivity.
proof:
For \(\alpha<\kappa^+\), the index set \(\alpha\) has cardinality at most
\(\kappa\). By T1, the cumulative union of the prior \(F_\beta\)'s has
triangle-cover number at most \(\kappa\). Apply T2.
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite, \(tc(G)>\kappa\), and
\(\langle F_\alpha:\alpha<\kappa^+\rangle\) be chosen adaptively so that
\(tc((V(G),F_\alpha))\le\kappa\) at every stage. For
\[
G_\alpha=G-\bigcup_{\beta<\alpha}F_\beta,
\]
one has \(tc(G_\alpha)>\kappa\) for every \(\alpha<\kappa^+\).
title: Successor-Length Adaptive Edge-Null Surgery

falsifier: At most \(2^κ\) induced κ-null vertex sets whose union induces triangle-cover number above κ.
proof:
Downward closure is immediate. Let \(\{A_i:i\in I\}\subseteq\mathcal J_\kappa(G)\)
with \(|I|\le2^\kappa\). Well-order \(I\) and disjointize the family:
\(P_i=A_i\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}A_j\). Every \(G[P_i]\) has triangle-cover
number at most \(\kappa\). Apply HG01 to the induced graph on
\(\bigcup_iA_i\), using the partition by the nonempty \(P_i\)'s and
\(\mu=\kappa\). Cardinal addition gives \(\kappa+\kappa=\kappa\).
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite and define
\[
\mathcal J_\kappa(G)=
\{A\subseteq V(G):tc(G[A])\le\kappa\}.
\]
Then \(\mathcal J_\kappa(G)\) is downward closed and closed under unions of
at most \(2^\kappa\) members.
title: The \(2^κ\)-Complete Induced-Null Vertex Ideal

falsifier: A high-cover graph made κ-coverable by deleting a vertex set inducing a κ-coverable graph.
novelty: "vertex deletion persistence" induced triangle-cover null set
proof:
Partition \(V(G)\) into \(A\) and \(V(G)\setminus A\). The cross-edge graph
is bipartite. If both induced sides had triangle-cover number at most
\(\kappa\), HG01 with two parts would give \(tc(G)\le\kappa\), a
contradiction.
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite. If \(tc(G)>\kappa\) and
\(A\in\mathcal J_\kappa(G)\), then
\[
tc(G-A)>\kappa.
\]
title: Induced-Null Vertex Deletion Persistence

falsifier: A partition into at most \(2^κ\) induced κ-null cells.
proof:
If every cell were in \(\mathcal J_\kappa(G)\), their union \(V(G)\) would
also lie in \(\mathcal J_\kappa(G)\) by HG04.
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite and \(tc(G)>\kappa\). Every partition of
\(V(G)\) into at most \(2^\kappa\) cells has a cell \(P\) satisfying
\[
tc(G[P])>\kappa.
\]
title: \(2^κ\)-Cell Vertex Indivisibility

falsifier: A κ-sized edge-profile partition all of whose cells are κ-coverable.
novelty: "simultaneous edge coloring" positive profile triangle cover
proof:
The combined profile map partitions \(E(G)\) into at most \(\kappa\) edge
sets. Apply HG02.
statement:
Let \(tc(G)>\kappa\), where \(\kappa\) is infinite. Suppose
\(\langle c_\xi:\xi<\lambda\rangle\) is a family of edge maps
\(c_\xi:E(G)\to X_\xi\) whose combined profile space has cardinality at most
\(\kappa\). Then some common profile class \(F\subseteq E(G)\) satisfies
\[
tc((V(G),F))>\kappa.
\]
In particular this holds for every finite family of \(\kappa\)-valued edge
colorings.
title: Finite/Small Edge-Profile Canonization

falsifier: At most κ many κ-valued unary labels with every common profile fiber κ-null.
proof:
Partition vertices by their combined profiles. The number of profiles is
at most \(\kappa^\lambda\le\kappa^\kappa=2^\kappa\); the last equality
follows from
\(2^\kappa\le\kappa^\kappa\le(2^\kappa)^\kappa=2^\kappa\).
Apply HG06.
statement:
Let \(\kappa\) be infinite and \(tc(G)>\kappa\). For every family
\[
\langle f_\xi:\xi<\lambda\rangle,\qquad \lambda\le\kappa,
\]
of vertex maps with \(|\operatorname{ran}(f_\xi)|\le\kappa\), there is
\(U\subseteq V(G)\) such that \(tc(G[U])>\kappa\) and every \(f_\xi\) is
constant on \(U\).
title: Simultaneous Unary Canonization

falsifier: A first stage below \((2^κ)^+\) at which induced-null vertex surgery destroys positivity.
proof:
For \(\alpha<\theta\), the prior family has cardinality at most \(2^\kappa\).
By HG04 its union belongs to \(\mathcal J_\kappa(G)\). Apply HG05.
Adaptivity is harmless because every chosen \(A_\beta\) lies in an induced
residual, so its induced graph is the same in the residual and in \(G\).
statement:
Let \(\theta=(2^\kappa)^+\), where \(\kappa\) is infinite and
\(tc(G)>\kappa\). Choose vertex sets \(A_\alpha\) adaptively for
\(\alpha<\theta\), with
\[
tc\!\left(G\!\left[A_\alpha\right]\right)\le\kappa.
\]
Then for every \(\alpha<\theta\),
\[
tc\!\left(G-\bigcup_{\beta<\alpha}A_\beta\right)>\kappa.
\]
title: Successor-of-\(2^κ\) Adaptive Vertex-Null Surgery

falsifier: A violation of either surgery theorem or the claimed completeness horizon.
proof:
Combine HG03 and HG09. The different horizons come from the
\(\kappa\)-completeness of the edge ideal and the \(2^\kappa\)-completeness
of the induced-null vertex ideal.
statement:
For a graph with \(tc(G)>\kappa\), adaptive deletion of κ-null edge sets is
guaranteed through every stage below \(\kappa^+\), whereas adaptive deletion
of induced κ-null vertex sets is guaranteed through every stage below
\((2^\kappa)^+\).
title: Dual Surgery Horizons

falsifier: A κ-sized unary profile system whose every common fiber is κ-null.
proof: This is the contrapositive interpretation of HG08.
statement:
No family of at most \(\kappa\) unary vertex invariants, each taking at most
\(\kappa\) values, can decompose a graph \(G\) with \(tc(G)>\kappa\) into
induced κ-null profile classes. One common profile class still has
triangle-cover number greater than \(\kappa\).
title: Unary-Profile Sterility Boundary

falsifier: A labeled K4-free high-cover graph with no profile-homogeneous high-chromatic link.
proof:
Apply HG08 to obtain a profile fiber \(U\) with
\(tc(G[U])>\kappa\). The induced graph \(G[U]\) is \(K_4\)-free. Apply T7
inside \(G[U]\). The extracted apex and its forward link remain inside
\(U\), so they have the same profile.
statement:
Let \(G\) be \(K_4\)-free with \(tc(G)>\kappa\), and let
\(\langle f_\xi:\xi<\lambda\rangle\), \(\lambda\le\kappa\), be
\(\kappa\)-valued vertex maps. There are a vertex \(v\), a triangle-free
induced subgraph \(L\subseteq N_G(v)\), and one common profile \(p\) such
that
\[
\chi(L)>\kappa
\]
and every vertex of \(\{v\}\cup V(L)\) has profile \(p\).
title: Canonized High-Chromatic Link Extraction

falsifier: A finite/small edge-profile system for which no positive profile subgraph has a high-chromatic link.
novelty: "edge profile" homogeneous high chromatic forward neighborhood
proof:
HG07 gives the positive edge-profile class. A subgraph of a \(K_4\)-free
graph is \(K_4\)-free. Apply T7 to \(G_F\).
statement:
Under the hypotheses of HG07, if \(G\) is also \(K_4\)-free, there is a
common edge-profile class \(F\) such that the spanning subgraph
\(G_F=(V(G),F)\) has triangle-cover number greater than \(\kappa\), and
\(G_F\) contains a triangle-free forward link of chromatic number greater
than \(\kappa\).
title: Edge-Profile Homogeneous Link Extraction

falsifier: A K4-free high-cover graph whose closed neighborhood of at most \(2^κ\) vertices meets every high-cover induced subgraph.
proof:
For each \(s\in S\), the induced graph \(G[N[s]]\) has triangle-cover
number at most two: use one layer for the star at \(s\) and one for the
triangle-free graph on \(N(s)\). Thus every \(N[s]\) belongs to
\(\mathcal J_\kappa(G)\). HG04 puts their union \(N[S]\) in the ideal, and
HG05 deletes it while preserving \(tc>\kappa\).
statement:
Let \(G\) be \(K_4\)-free with \(tc(G)>\kappa\), where \(\kappa\) is
infinite. If \(S\subseteq V(G)\) and \(|S|\le2^\kappa\), then
\[
tc(G-N_G[S])>\kappa.
\]
title: Closed-Neighborhood Escape Beyond \(2^κ\)

falsifier: A first stage below \((2^κ)^+\) where the disjoint high-link cone recursion fails.
novelty: "2^kappa successor" disjoint high chromatic cones K4-free
proof:
Recurse on \(\alpha<\theta\). Every previously chosen cone induces a graph
of triangle-cover number two, so its vertex set belongs to
\(\mathcal J_\kappa(G)\). Before stage \(\alpha\), there are at most
\(2^\kappa\) such sets. HG04 and HG05 leave a positive induced residual
disjoint from all previous cones. Apply T7 in that residual.
statement:
Let \(\theta=(2^\kappa)^+\). Every \(K_4\)-free graph \(G\) with
\(tc(G)>\kappa\) contains \(\theta\) pairwise vertex-disjoint induced cones
\[
K_1\vee L_\alpha\qquad(\alpha<\theta),
\]
where every \(L_\alpha\) is triangle-free and
\(\chi(L_\alpha)>\kappa\).
title: Massive Vertex-Disjoint High-Link Cone Packing

falsifier: A first stage below \((2^κ)^+\) at which closed-neighborhood escape, link extraction, or finite-color compactness fails.
proof:
At stage \(\alpha\), the union \(S_\alpha\) of the earlier finite cones has
cardinality at most \(2^\kappa\). HG14 supplies a positive induced residual
inside \(G-N[S_\alpha]\), hence anticomplete to every earlier cone. Apply T7
to obtain a triangle-free link of chromatic number greater than \(\kappa\).
The de Bruijn–Erdős compactness theorem yields a finite induced subgraph of
chromatic number greater than \(f(\alpha)\); minimize its vertex set to get
the critical graph \(Q_\alpha\), and adjoin the apex.
statement:
Let \(\theta=(2^\kappa)^+\), let \(G\) be \(K_4\)-free with
\(tc(G)>\kappa\), and let \(f:\theta\to\omega\). Then \(G\) contains a
pairwise anticomplete family of induced cones
\[
K_1\vee Q_\alpha\qquad(\alpha<\theta),
\]
where every \(Q_\alpha\) is finite, triangle-free, vertex-critical, and
\(\chi(Q_\alpha)>f(\alpha)\).
title: Massive Pairwise-Anticomplete Critical-Cone Packing

falsifier: A verified prescribed-tree premise and a first failed stage of the anticomplete cone recursion.
novelty: "prescribed sequence" pairwise anticomplete tree cones Erdős 738 595
proof:
Repeat the recursion in HG16, replacing the finite-critical extraction by
the assumed induced-tree theorem inside the high-chromatic triangle-free
link at each stage.
statement:
Let \(\theta=(2^\kappa)^+\) and let
\(\langle T_\alpha:\alpha<\theta\rangle\) be finite trees such that every
triangle-free graph of chromatic number greater than \(\kappa\) contains an
induced \(T_\alpha\). Then every \(K_4\)-free graph \(G\) with
\(tc(G)>\kappa\) contains pairwise anticomplete induced cones
\[
K_1\vee T_\alpha\qquad(\alpha<\theta).
\]
title: Conditional Massive Prescribed Tree-Cone Packing

falsifier: A family of at most κ maximal layers whose complete common-book support cannot be evicted.
novelty: "common omitted edge" stable certificate page eviction
proof:
T10 and T9 make every \(W_i\) nonempty and stable. The sets \(W_i\) and the
two singletons all belong to \(\mathcal J_\kappa(G)\); there are at most
\(\kappa\) of them. HG04 puts their union in the ideal, and HG05 deletes it
while preserving positivity.
statement:
Let \(G\) be \(K_4\)-free with \(tc(G)>\kappa\), and let
\(\{H_i:i\in I\}\) be maximal spanning triangle-free subgraphs with
\(|I|\le\kappa\). Choose the common omitted edge \(xy\) supplied by T10 and
put \(W_i=N_{H_i}(x)\cap N_{H_i}(y)\). Then
\[
tc\!\left(G-\left(\{x,y\}\cup\bigcup_{i\in I}W_i\right)\right)>\kappa.
\]
title: Complete Stable-Certificate Page Eviction

falsifier: A first proper stage below \((2^κ)^+\) at which repeated complete-book eviction destroys positivity.
proof:
Each stage support is an induced κ-null vertex set by the proof of HG18.
Apply the adaptive vertex-null surgery theorem HG09.
statement:
Let \(\theta=(2^\kappa)^+\) and \(G\) be \(K_4\)-free with
\(tc(G)>\kappa\). At every stage \(\alpha<\theta\), in the current induced
residual choose at most \(\kappa\) maximal spanning triangle-free layers,
form their common omitted-edge certificate support as in HG18, and delete
that support. Every proper-stage residual still has triangle-cover number
greater than \(\kappa\).
title: Successor-of-\(2^κ\) Common-Book Eviction Process

falsifier: A κ-sized unary label system for which no profile contains the asserted anticomplete critical-cone civilization.
novelty: "canonized" pairwise anticomplete critical cones unary profiles
proof:
HG08 supplies an induced positive profile fiber \(U\). Apply HG16 to
\(G[U]\). Every resulting vertex remains in \(U\), so all labels are
constant on the entire packing.
statement:
Under the hypotheses of HG08 and with \(G\) \(K_4\)-free, there is one
common unary profile \(p\) and a family of
\((2^\kappa)^+\) pairwise anticomplete induced cones
\(K_1\vee Q_\alpha\) such that every vertex of every cone has profile \(p\),
and the \(Q_\alpha\)'s meet arbitrary prescribed finite chromatic thresholds.
title: Canonized Pairwise-Anticomplete Critical-Cone Packing

falsifier: A specified layer/signature system for which every page-free common profile fiber is κ-null.
proof:
Use HG18 to delete the complete common-book support while retaining a
positive induced residual. Restrict the unary maps to that residual and
apply HG08.
statement:
Let \(G\) be \(K_4\)-free with \(tc(G)>\kappa\). Fix at most \(\kappa\)
maximal spanning triangle-free layers and at most \(\kappa\)
\(\kappa\)-valued unary vertex maps. Then there are:
1. a common omitted edge and its stable certificate pages for the layers;
2. an induced subgraph \(G[U]\) with \(tc(G[U])>\kappa\);
such that \(U\) avoids the two endpoints and every certificate page, while
all unary maps are constant on \(U\).
title: Canonized Page-Free Subwitness

falsifier: A layer/signature system whose page-free canonized subwitness lacks the massive anticomplete critical-cone packing.
proof: Apply HG16 inside the induced subwitness produced by HG21.
statement:
Under the hypotheses of HG21, the page-free common profile subwitness
contains \((2^\kappa)^+\) pairwise anticomplete induced critical cones,
all of whose vertices share the same unary profile and avoid the original
common-book certificate support.
title: Fully Canonized Page-Free Cone Civilization

falsifier: A proof of full Erdős #738 and a high-cover K4-free graph lacking the stated universal anticomplete cone family.
proof:
Enumerate the countable set of finite trees along a sequence of length
\(\theta\) so that each tree appears \(\theta\) times, and apply HG17.
statement:
Assume Erdős #738 holds for every finite tree. Let
\(\theta=(2^\kappa)^+\). Every \(K_4\)-free graph \(G\) with
\(tc(G)>\kappa\) contains a pairwise anticomplete family of induced cones
of size \(\theta\) in which every finite tree occurs as the cone base
\(\theta\) times.
title: Conditional Universal Finite-Tree Cone Civilization
